message.content: {"caption":"Three-panel diagram comparing multi-session dog-adoption dialogue handling by a vanilla LLM and an RL-finetuned LLM.","description":"The left, blue-tinted panel, titled “Multi-session dialogues,” shows two sessions. In the first, a blue speech bubble says, “Hi Audrey! I recently adopted a pup from a shelter. I named him Buddy.” A yellow reply says, “That's perfect, Andrew!” A vertical dashed divider labeled “Another day, new session” separates it from a second blue bubble: “I can't help myself but to adopt another dog. His name is Scout.” A final yellow reply says, “That's great news!” The middle, pink-tinted panel, titled “Vanilla LLM as backbone,” starts with a purple box labeled “Current Memory Bank” holding “Andrew adopted a new dog from a shelter and named him Buddy.” Under “In-context Memory Manager,” a chip-like icon accompanies two red operation boxes: “DELETE: Andrew adopted a new dog from a shelter and named him Buddy.” and “ADD: Andrew adopted a new dog and named the pup Scout.” A red X marks this memory-management outcome. Below a horizontal dashed divider, a box says “Retrieved: <Memory 1> ... <Memory 60>” and “Question: How many dogs have Andrew adopted?” Under “LLM generate response,” another chip-like icon accompanies the red response “Answer: 1 dog,” marked with a red X. Red explanatory text says this misinterprets the different dog names as a conflict and overwrites the original memory. The right, green-tinted panel, titled “RL-finetuned LLM as backbone,” begins with the same current memory bank. Under “Memory Manager,” a database-and-bot icon accompanies a green box: “UPDATE: Andrew adopted 2 dogs named Buddy and Scout.” A green check marks this outcome. Below a horizontal dashed divider, the same retrieved-memory range and question appear. Under “Answer Agent with Memory Distillation,” a brain-and-bot icon accompanies a green box reading “Useful memories for answering the question: <Memory 1> Answer: 2 dogs,” marked with a green check. Green explanatory text says the second dog's name is interpreted as an addition and the memory is updated to reflect both adoptions. The panels present dialogue first, then memory handling and answering; no arrows are shown.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
